_source: docs/04 §8 (Backstories): §8.1's four-field format, §8.3's eighteen reusable tags with their 'Bullet reads like' and 'Listens for' columns, and §8.1's draw rules. Canon anchor: raw notes, Morale — 'Gaining and losing Morale will be based on their back stories largely we can have bullet points for each raider that is recruited'.
_notes: docs/04 §8.3's rule for this file, verbatim: 'Every tag must be listenable, or it does not ship.' The `listens` field on every tag below is that column, kept so a reader can check the claim rather than trust it.
docs/04 §8.1: 'Written per-tag with 3-6 variants for variety.' Every tag carries four, so no tag is the one that always reads the same.
The `tag` is 'the only field doc 05 reads' (§8.1). `polarity` drives the card icon and §8.1's per-rarity draw rules; `weight` is docs/05's multiplier on that raider's own delta.
docs/04 §8.3 tag 6 is `class_rival:<class>` — parameterised, so it is stored once here and the class is bound at draw time.
Bullets are written in the third person and about the RAIDER, never about a real person: docs/04 §7's content-review standard covers this file too.
_exclusion_notes: docs/04 §8.1 names the first two pairs. The other two are the same rule applied to the contradictions §8.3's own table creates: a raider cannot both cry at every wipe and call wipes 'data', and cannot both notice last tier's gear and offer to raid naked.

`resents_authority` is not one of §8.3's eighteen tags — the doc names it only in the exclusion rule. It is kept in the graph so the rule survives the day that tag ships, and the loader ignores pairs naming a tag it does not have.

tags.listens: Run resolves with this raider not in the 12
variants: Left his last guild over a bench decision.
Keeps a written record of every night he sat out.
Asked, twice, what the bench is for.
Says he understands. He does not understand.

tags.listens: Loot awarded — to self (up) or to another raider of the same class (down)
variants: Openly here for the gear. Says so in the interview.
Asked about the loot rules before asking your name.
Has a list. The list is gear.
Would leave for a better shield. Told you so, unprompted.

tags.listens: Reputation rank increase; any raid win
variants: Has your old raid logs printed out.
Refers to you, in writing, as 'the boss'.
Joined the day he heard you were recruiting.
Tells other guilds about this one. At length.

tags.listens: Raid wipe with this raider present
variants: Cries during wipes. Every wipe.
Goes very quiet for a day after a bad night.
Asked whether dying hurts. Was not joking.
Counts the wipes. Out loud, afterwards.

tags.listens: Raid wipe with this raider present
variants: Calls every wipe 'data'.
Has died more times than he can count and finds that funny.
Was the only one laughing.
Says the floor is a valid strategy.

tags.listens: Named class present in the same raid roster
variants: Refuses to speak to {class}s.
Has a long-standing grievance with {class}s. Will explain it.
Was, he says, wronged by a {class}. Once.
Will not stand next to a {class}.

tags.listens: A rostered raider departs or is fired / is in the same raid
variants: Only joined because his mate did.
Does not raid well alone. Says he does.
Asked who else was coming before saying yes.
Brought someone to the interview for support.

tags.listens: This raider was top of their role's contribution in a run
variants: Wants his name said out loud after fights.
Keeps his own numbers. Shares them.
Asked whether there is a leaderboard.
Describes his best night to anyone who stands still.

tags.listens: Every run start (self-inflicted, always fires small)
variants: Was late to the interview.
Has never once been on time, and is always surprised.
Owns a clock. Its purpose is decorative.
Arrives as the pull starts. Every time.

tags.listens: Own equipment contains an item below CT at run start
variants: Notices when someone is wearing last tier.
Will not wear anything he considers beneath him.
Made a comment about the boots. It was not kind.
Asked whether the guild has standards.

tags.listens: Own equipment below CT at run start (no penalty; small positive when passing loot)
variants: Would raid naked. Has offered to.
Genuinely does not know what he is wearing.
Passes on upgrades without being asked.
Says the gear is not the point. Means it.

tags.listens: Role assignment for the run does not include a tank slot for them
variants: Insists he is a tank. He is not.
Stands in front regardless of instruction.
Has strong opinions about being hit, all of them wrong.
Asked for the tank slot before giving his name.

tags.listens: First attempt of a boss; attempt number is a multiple of 13
variants: Will not pull without saying the thing.
Has a lucky item. It does nothing.
Refuses to count the attempts out loud.
Turns around three times before every boss.

tags.listens: runs_attended crosses each multiple of 5 without a rest week
variants: Talks about going home a lot.
Has a letter he has not opened in weeks.
Asks, every few nights, how long this goes on for.
Says the guildhall does not smell like anywhere.

tags.listens: Guild gold below a threshold at payday
variants: Being followed by someone he owes.
Asked when payday is, then asked again.
Sold his old guild's tabard. It was not his.
Winces at the word 'interest'.

tags.listens: Comfort item purchased; guild facility upgraded
variants: Has a tab. It is large.
Knows the tavern staff by name. All of them.
Considers the tavern part of the guildhall.
Was recruited at the bar and has not really left.

tags.listens: A Common or Uncommon raider is recruited
variants: Keeps trying to teach the new people.
Wrote a guide. Nobody asked. It is quite good.
Takes the worst raider aside after every wipe.
Says he was terrible once too, and is not lying.

tags.listens: This raider dies during an encounter
variants: Has a theory about why he died.
Says he was not healed. He was healed.
Checks the healing numbers before checking his own.
Died standing in the fire, and has questions for the Cleric.
